Data: CRU
Spot premium quotations for imported cathode fell sharply in the past two weeks as a result of a closing of the import arbitrage window and the related widening of cathode import loss. We heard reports that spot premium quotations for imported cathode declined to $50-100/t last week and further contracted to $30-80/t this week as major traders offered cathode at $70-80/t while some traders who import cathode as collateral for financing offered material at around $30/t as they sought a quick sale under the expectation that the SHFE/LME negative arbitrage will persist in the short term. However, we heard very few deals were closed. In addition, some © 2012 CRU International Limited **confidential** **February 2012** www.crugroup.com copper smelters planned to engage in copper concentrate tolling business, which means that they intend to export cathode given the favorable SHFE/LME price ratio. We were told by market participants that cathode inventories in Shanghai bonded warehouses currently amount to 370,000t-380,000t, indicating a rise of 35,000t over the past two weeks, which was attributed to traders attempting to circumvent incurring losses through the sale of imported metal on the spot market. Market participants expect the SHFE/LME arbitrage window may re-open in April as a result of a fall in cathode import volumes and increased exports from smelters in the coming months. Moreover, cathode demand may improve as the seasonally strong second quarter approaches. Alternatively, the SHFE/LME arbitrage window may reopen in advance of this if the LME copper price is weakened by financial market turmoil. # **Smelters to engage in the copper concentrate tolling business** According to reports, several copper smelters are planning to engage in copper concentrate processing trade, also known as copper tolling. They could make a profit through copper tolling, although given the currently negative SHFE/LME arbitrage the smelters would be exporting and they would need to pay a 3% export value tax. China’s Ministry of Commerce reintroduced copper tolling in February 2009 after it had been prohibited for over 2 years. The 3% tolling tax was designed as a relief tax to smelters to replace a 17% import value-added tax and a 5%-10% refined copper export tax, in or

der to allow them to engage in tolling services. Seven copper smelters, Jiangxi Copper, Yunnan Copper, Tongling Nonferrous, Jinchuan Group, Daye Nonferrous, Baiyin Nonferrous and Yanggu Xiangguang Copper, are currently authorised to engage in concentrate tolling. The tolling quota is fixed at 20-30% of a smelter’s concentrate import tonnage in the previous year. We expect China’s cathode exports or cathode inventory in Shanghai bonded warehouse may increase before the SHFE/LME arbitrage window re-opens. # **Decline in scrap imports in January** SHFE inventoryChinese importsheads higher (000t)of scrap (monthly)

Jan/10 May/10 Sep/10 Jan/11 May/11 Sep/11 Jan/12 According to Chinese customs preliminary data, China’s imports of scrap in January amounted to 230,000t, down 48.5% m-o-m and 37.0% y-o-y. We understand there are several factors behind the significant import decline. The most important reason is that scrap import activity was affected by the week-long Lunar New Year holiday in January. Similarly, in 2011, the holiday was in February and monthly import figures declined by 22,000t compared February 2010. Data: GTIS © 2012 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 4 **February 2012** www.crugroup.com Another factor is that scrap traders’ import enthusiasm was constrained as copper price uncertainties have persisted causing fears that prices will decline in Q1 2012. Finally, scrap traders were affected by new measures implemented by the Chinese government to prevent the transfer and re-sale of scrap import permits. We believe that some small sized scrap traders, whose import permits have been bought or transferred from other traders, will be affected in the short term. However, the overall level of scrap imports will not be affected as large and middle sized scrap traders will continue their import activities. Nevertheless, we expect that China’s scrap imports will remain at low levels in February due to the negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME. # **Copper prices continue to be affected by financial sentiments** SHFE inventory continued to increase

The LME 3-month copper price continued to be affected by the financial turmoil over the past two weeks. The price declined to below $8,300/t this Friday due to the delays in the critical bailout fund for Greece. In addition, weak physical buying in China affected market sentiment. The SHFE 3-month copper price fluctuated in a range of RMB59,210-60,550/t. We noticed that the Shanghai physical discount widened again after 15th February when the SHFE cash month contra

ct changed, which indicated weak domestic demand and abundant cathode supply. According to the latest report, the SHFE cathode inventory rose to 217,142t this week, up 37,251t compared to two weeks ago. 

We believe that the domestic market insiders may begin de-stocking refined copper in the short term, following a period of re-stocking in late 2011 and early 2012.  At the same time, the significant negative arbitrage between SHFE and LME will continue to constrain all types of copper imports into China including concentrate, scrap and cathode.  The decreased supply coupled with recovering demand in end Q1 and early Q2 2012 will provide support for copper prices.  However, in the short term we do not expect copper prices to rise.  The SHFE 3-month copper prices are expected to be trade in the range RMB57,500-60,000/t.
